messages.subject: iterative purification DIF procedure without known anchor items
messages.subject_clean: iterative purification DIF procedure without known anchor items
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am trying to use the mirt package for my dissertation to examine DIF of a screening scale across gender and racial groups. I'm having trouble finding a "translated" method from the iterative procedure proposed by Tay et al. (2015) "An overview and practical guide to IRT measurement equivalence analysis", when non-DIF items are identified as anchor items and then used to put the reference and focal groups on the same scale for subsequent DIF analyses. The authors used IRTPRO for their analyses and I would like to use this procedure, but using the mirt package in R.

These are the steps outlined in Tay et al. (2015):
1. constraining all items to be equal across group(s) and estimating the latent trait distributions (mean and variance) for the focal group(s)
2. focal group(s) trait distributions are fixed at values found in Step 1 and item parameters are freely estimated across groups

Can this procedure be done with the mirt package?

I have seen other methods that use all other items as anchor items in the first reference model to identify anchor items, is this analogous to the iterative procedure?

Thank you for any help in advance!
Anna

messages.subject: shiny apps..io hosting
messages.body_plain:
Good morning all,

I have been attempting to get a CAT up and running for my lab, but it is proving to be very difficult. I have spent quite some time troubleshooting code over the past few weeks and would like to publicly host an adaptive survey I made. When I "select all" and "run" my code through R the code launches my browser and it looks great! When I exit my web browser and return to R my viewer window opens and displays the survey, but it has all the default mirtCAT GUI settings. When I "publish" the survey I get an error and a failure to launch. Here is a summary of my problems:

1. The GUI in my viewer window is the mirtCAT default.
2. Publishing a white screen with "An error has occurred"

I have attached the log for my shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> if that will help, there is an error of "cannot change working directory"

Any help would be greatly appreciated! I am new to R and mirtCAT and I could use some teaching in this area if anyone would be willing to help. I appreciate it!

Best,
Alec

Hello,

Thank you for all the information you share in this group. I want to use the Rasch model to concurrently estimate item difficulties in the following scenario: I have three test forms, X1, X2, and X3, administered to three different groups. X1 and X2 share common items. X3 does not share any items with either X1 or X2, but it shares common test takers with X2. I believe I should use the multipleGroup function, but I get stuck on the specifics. How can I specify the common people between the groups?

Kind Regards,
Eren Asena
